name: Guitar Pro (mobile)
complaints: No Android update since ~2022 (last major update May 2020, v1.6.3); users asking if abandoned
Very crashy — 'open a tab from a popular website? crash'; lacks compatibility with modern phones
Soundbanks 'like from GP5', clunky menus, can't write multi-track, file corruption in NotePad
Paid app treated as 'a second thought' vs desktop Guitar Pro; users say it should cost $1-2 for what it does
freeIncumbentRisk: Low-medium: Songsterr/UG cover tab playback but nothing free properly renders/plays .gp files offline; guitarists demonstrably pay for this job
moatNotes: The .gp file-format player/practice niche is captive: huge existing libraries of GP files, desktop users need a mobile companion. Arobas showed a new-app prototype at NAMM 2025 but nothing shipped — clone window open but time-limited

name: FL Studio Mobile
complaints: Crashes constantly on Android — on opening projects, tapping Overview, mid-song, losing work
Compatibility problems with newer Android versions acknowledged in Image-Line's own troubleshooting docs/forums
Perceived neglect: Image-Line's attention is on desktop FL Studio; mobile UI/engine felt frozen for years
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: BandLab is free and strong for beginners, but a serious offline one-time-purchase pocket DAW (the thing people paid $15 for) has no healthy incumbent; Caustic is abandoned, Audio Evolution is niche
moatNotes: 1M+ people paid $15 up front for a mobile DAW — proven willingness to pay in a category where the leader ships crashes. Brand is the moat to beat; win on stability + modern-Android audio latency

name: Alight Motion
price: Free, paid-gated (watermark + core features behind ~$30-60/yr subscription)
complaints: Trial/subscription traps: 'trial still takes money even when you press X to decline'; charges after unsubscribing
Paywall screens users can't close without purchasing; must start a trial to even use the app
Bending Spoons acquisition amplified aggressive monetization resentment; refund friction
freeIncumbentRisk: HIGH: CapCut covers casual editing free. But Alight's niche is keyframe/vector motion graphics + shareable project presets, which CapCut doesn't really serve — a fair one-time-purchase motion-graphics editor targets the angry 3.59-star base
moatNotes: Massive community of 'AM preset' creators (XML project sharing) locked into a hated pricing model; import-compat or preset ecosystem would be the wedge

name: VSCO: Photo & Video Editor
complaints: Bait-and-switch: presets bought as one-time purchases pre-2017 went gray and now require a subscription — purchases converted into rentals
7-day trial 'falsely claimed' — users report immediate charges and 'not our problem' support responses
Plus tier price roughly doubled from the old $19.99/yr model; stability complaints on Android
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: Snapseed/Lightroom free tier edit photos free, but the film-emulation preset aesthetic is exactly what people paid VSCO for; a one-time-purchase film-preset editor directly answers the top complaint
moatNotes: Angriest large install base in mobile photo editing; the winning pitch is literally 'buy your film presets once, keep them forever' — the promise VSCO broke

name: Adobe Premiere Rush
price: Freemium, paid-gated (premium sub via Creative Cloud)
complaints: Officially abandoned: delisted from stores Sept 30 2025, app killed Sept 30 2026; last Android update Sept 2024
Android users stranded — replacement 'Premiere on iPhone' is iOS-only, Premiere for Android has no release date
Users who reinstalled phones can no longer download an app they paid Creative Cloud money to use
freeIncumbentRisk: HIGH: CapCut/YouTube Create serve casual users free. The residual demand is 'prosumer timeline editor with desktop-class export, no watermark, no TikTok data concerns', which is narrower but pays
moatNotes: 5M Android installs of a pro-brand editor with the vendor publicly exiting and telling Android users to wait indefinitely; a stable one-time-purchase prosumer editor can harvest the diaspora — but must clearly beat free CapCut on trust/watermark/ownership

name: Photo Mate R3 (RAW editor)
price: Free, paid-gated (IAP to unlock full features/ad-free)
complaints: Solo-dev app dating to 2016 with long dormant stretches; users experienced years-stale RAW camera profiles and modern-device breakage before sporadic revivals (latest update Dec 2025)
Rating decayed to 3.53 while remaining one of the only full RAW workflow (Lightroom-style) editors on Android
freeIncumbentRisk: HIGH: Lightroom Mobile's free tier edits RAW. The payable gap is offline/no-account/one-time-purchase RAW culling+editing for photographers who refuse Adobe subscriptions
moatNotes: Small but real: desktop-class RAW batch workflow on Android tablets has no healthy paid incumbent; smallest install base on this list, treat as niche bet
